Chapter 3: Chasing Dreams in a World That Doesn’t Understand
Leaving home for college’s always a big step. But when you’ve never quite felt like you fit in, it can feel downright overwhelming.
The campus—well, it was its own little universe. So many new faces, unfamiliar routines, and expectations that felt impossible to pin down. Suddenly, that old pressure to succeed came rushing back, stirring up insecurities she thought she’d left behind. Would anyone really get her love for gaming and fantasy? Was she going to keep up with the fast pace of college life?
Honestly, the beginning wasn’t easy. All those unwritten social rules made everything confusing, and there was always that worry about standing out for the wrong reasons. So, she dove into her coursework, determined to prove she belonged. Even her violin, which used to bring so much comfort, started to weigh her down. The joy of playing faded under the pressure to meet everyone else’s expectations. There were days when giving up seemed a whole lot easier than pushing through.
But the internet? That was her lifeline. After long evenings of studying, she’d slip into the familiar glow of her favorite forums and games. The friendships she’d built online were a steady source of support, a place where she could drop the mask and just be herself. Those late-night chats and inside jokes kept her going, even when real life felt like too much.
Then one night, after a particularly tough week, something changed. She met a group of students who actually shared her interests. They geeked out over sci-fi and gaming, and before long, late-night gaming sessions became their thing. For the first time, she felt that spark of belonging in the real world. It was thrilling—and a little scary. Turns out, she wasn’t the only one who valued creativity and curiosity over just fitting in.
Most people don’t see just how much courage it takes to chase a dream that doesn’t fit the usual script. The road’s almost never straight, and the hurdles can feel huge. She faced her share—failed auditions, rejections, and those familiar waves of self-doubt. That nagging voice saying, “You’re not good enough,” was never far away.
Still, her drive to create and connect was stronger than her fear. The internet opened up a world of possibilities—a place where passion projects could find their people and quirky ideas could actually take root. The lesson? Sometimes, what makes you different is exactly what’ll help you stand out and thrive.
As graduation loomed, the pressure to pick a “safe” path got louder. Family and friends meant well, nudging her toward something practical. But deep down, she knew she couldn’t ignore the pull of creativity. Settling for a life that didn’t feel true to who she was? That just wasn’t an option. In the end, it became clear: the only way forward was to lean into her weirdness, no matter how risky it seemed.
